chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Is'haq, from Abi Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said:

I said to Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام): "Your majesty prevents me from asking you, so will you permit me to ask you?" He said: "Ask." I said: "O my master, do you have a son?" He said: "Yes." I said: "If an event occurs to you, then where shall I ask about him?" He said: "In al-Madinah."

key_terms.حَدَثٌ: an occurrence, here referring to death or a grave event

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith from al-Kafi indicate the existence of a son of Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith records a companion asking Imam Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) about whether he had a son, and the Imam confirms that he did. The report is significant in discussions of the Imamate, as it presents an indication toward the existence of the succeeding Imam and where he would be sought.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary who said,

‘I said to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) ‘Your<sup>asws</sup> majesty prevents me from asking you<sup>asws</sup>, so if you<sup>asws</sup> were to permit me, I shall ask you<sup>asws</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ask’. I said, ‘O my Chief! Is there a son<sup>asws</sup> for you<sup>asws</sup>?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. So I said, ‘So if there occurs with you an occurrence (of death), so where shall I ask about him<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘At Al-Medina’’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from abu Hashim al-Ja‘fari who has said the following.

“I said to abu Muhammad (a.s.), ‘Your grace causes shyness to me to ask you questions. May I ask you a question?” He said, “Yes, you may ask.” I said, “My master, do you have a son?” He said, “Yes, I do have a son.” I then said, “If anything will happen to you, where would I ask him (about my religion)?” He replied, “Ask him in Madina.”
